messages.text: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit

metadata.summary: Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.
metadata.content: European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content European Championship Darts: Ross Smith beats Martin Schindler to Dortmund title after Luke Littler's quarter-final exit Luke Littler suffered a quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajski, extending his wait for his elusive ranked TV title; Ross Smith beat Martin Schindler in the European Championship final; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 25 October 2026 23:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the winning moment from Ross Smith's European Championship success, where he closed out an 11-8 victory over Martin Schindler. (Credit: ITV) Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund. The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen. Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw. metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix.
metadata.content: United States GP: Kimi Antonelli wins Austin race to move to brink of F1 world title after dominant drive | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: Kimi Antonelli wins Austin race to move to brink of F1 world title after dominant drive Kimi Antonelli delivers emphatic victory in Austin to move a maximum of two points away from clinching 2026's Drivers' Championship; Antonelli only needs a ninth-place finish next Sunday in Mexico to be sure; Charles Leclerc's late surge secures second place in race from Max Verstappen Sunday 25 October 2026 23:41, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix. Antonelli had an outside chance of clinching the 2026 title as early as Sunday's Austin race provided he won, Lewis Hamilton finished outside the top four and George Russell was ninth or lower. And while he held up his side of the bargain by brilliantly claiming a ninth win of the season on a one-stop strategy to his nearest rivals' two, Hamilton took fourth and Russell eighth to stay in mathematical contention. metadata.summary: Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is hanging by a thread.
metadata.content: Michael Carrick Man Utd future: Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann expected frontrunners if head coach departs | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Michael Carrick Man Utd future: Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann expected frontrunners if head coach departs Man Utd beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford to heap the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick; Captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped and United are eight games without a win Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Sunday 25 October 2026 21:49, UK Image: Michael Carrick waves to supporters at Old Trafford after his team's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach is hanging by a thread. United plunged to a new low on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth . The defeat extends their winless run to eight matches and leaves United just above the Premier League relegation zone. Sky Sports News understands that United's bosses were already considering alternatives for the head coach role even before the defeat to Bournemouth amid the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League season. messages.text: Neville fears Carrick set to be sacked as Carra calls for swift decision

metadata.summary: Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher.
metadata.content: Manchester United: Michael Carrick head coach on brink of losing job after Bournemouth defeat | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Manchester United: Michael Carrick head coach on brink of losing job after Bournemouth defeat Man Utd suffered a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday; Michael Carrick's future is in doubt after a eighth game without a win in all competitions Sunday 25 October 2026 22:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking immediately after Manchester United's defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League, Gary Neville gives his thoughts on Michael Carrick's future Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher. The humbling defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season. "It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary. On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him." Carrick struck a defiant tone after the game but his lengthy applause towards the United fans after the final whistle was immediately interpreted as a farewell gesture.
